semantics.label: What to practise
semantics.description: With «Choose when starting», whoever plays picks it on the first screen: handy in the middle of a class.

options.label: Equalities: sums with the gap on either side
Free balance, for the board, with no points

semantics.label: How the scale moves
semantics.description: Free is what works best in studies with on-screen balances: the scale leans and the equality changes at the same time (Otten, Van den Heuvel-Panhuizen and Veldhuis, 2019, a review of 34 studies, https://doi.org/10.1186/s40594-019-0183-2). Points: 2 if it balances without taking any weight off, 1 with one or two taken off. Held makes players decide before they check: for those who already know the equal sign well.

options.label: Held: it stays still until it is let go

semantics.label: The scale
semantics.description: The market suits younger children best and the notebook, older ones. If players choose, they see only the picture and the name, with no age.

semantics.label: Fine tuning
semantics.description: Optional. Where the game starts; it moves up a level with three good rounds in a row.
